findings.evidence: Plan structure: Overview, Prerequisites, Phases with tasks, Testing Strategy, Dependency Graph, Risks, Rollback. ... Tasks must be small and independently testable
findings.fix: Cut the generic plan-section list to the parts Codex would not choose by itself (Dependencies as task IDs for parallel work, Complexity 1-10, Test-First Approach per task). The model already writes Overview, Risks and Rollback without being told.

findings.evidence: Read what the plan depends on: README, manifests, config, the code to be extended, schemas, test patterns, docs.
findings.fix: Keep only the verified-paths rule ('the prompt may cite nothing else'). The list of file kinds to read is generic context-gathering the model already does.

findings.evidence: Sort what you know into confirmed requirements, blocking decisions (they change the plan's shape: stack, scope, auth method) and non-blocking assumptions.
findings.fix: Add a short test for blocking decisions, for example: 'Before asking, ask yourself: would Codex produce a structurally different phase list under each answer? If not, record it as an assumption.' That turns the sorting step into a reusable thinking framework.

findings.evidence: - Reply in English unless the user asks otherwise.
findings.fix: Give this item a reason (for example, the Codex prompt and plan file stay in English so the user can pass them on), or move it out of Gotchas. It is a preference, not an environment fact that defies assumptions.

findings.evidence: ## Gotchas (no item on Codex prompt-size or sandbox limits)
findings.fix: Add a Codex-specific gotcha you learned the hard way, for example: 'NEVER tell Codex to run tests or install packages in the prompt: under -s workspace-write network is off and the plan run stalls or fails.'

findings.evidence: description: Prepare prompt_to_codex.md so the user can run Codex themselves and get an implementation plan in codex-plan.md. Use when planning a feature, API, auth change, migration or test strategy, including underspecified requests.
findings.fix: Prepare prompt_to_codex.md so the user can run the OpenAI Codex CLI (codex exec) themselves and get an implementation plan in codex-plan.md. Use when the user wants a Codex-written plan, a hand-off prompt for Codex, or a plan for a feature, API, auth change, migration or test strategy, including underspecified requests. Gathers repo context, asks only blocking questions, shows the manual command. Not for implementing changes or running Codex; never runs Codex.

findings.evidence: Plan structure: Overview, Prerequisites, Phases with tasks, Testing Strategy, Dependency Graph, Risks, Rollback.
findings.fix: Make the section list a default with an escape hatch: 'Drop Rollback or Dependency Graph when they do not apply (for example, a pure test-strategy plan).' A fixed section set for every plan type is more rigid than this low-consequence step needs.

findings.evidence: Ask the user to send you the content of `codex-plan.md` when Codex finishes. Do nothing else until they do, and never guess what the plan says.
findings.fix: Add what happens after the plan comes back, for example: 'When the user pastes it, check that every confirmed requirement maps to a task with acceptance criteria and list any gaps; do not start implementing unless asked.' Also cover the case where Codex fails or writes no file (ask for the Codex output and rerun guidance).

findings.evidence: If either exists, ask whether to overwrite or use a `-2` suffix (both names); never overwrite silently.
findings.fix: Resolve the case where the -2 names also exist: 'increment the suffix (-3, -4, ...) until both names are free.' Add how to detect a non-git directory for line 29 (`git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`).
